newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Japan asks for Indonesia tariff cut on car imports.
newsitem.headline: Japan asks for Indonesia tariff cut on car imports.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday that Japanese officials had asked for a cut in import tariffs on automobiles brought into the country and that the proposal was being studied.
Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo told reporters that the suggestion came up during talks between trade officials of both countries at a meeting in Tokyo last week.
The two sides met to discuss Indonesia's controversial national car policy, which Japan, the United States and the European Union say is biased against imports from their regions.

"I reported to the president about the progress of the negotiating team," Ariwibowo said after a meeting with President Suharto. "There are things that have been proposed by Japan. The proposals are about tax and import duties."
"We will study the proposals but we must see our national interest too," he said.
Ariwibowo said Indonesia was preparing for economic deregulation, including cutting import tariffs, and was studying whether the Japanese proposals were in line with Jakarta's policy.
Ariwibowo said the Indonesian negotiating team held talks with Japanese officials in Tokyo on June 5-6.
"Currently the team is in Geneva to meet European Union officials to discuss Indonesia's car policy," he added.

Indonesia's national car policy gives PT Timor Putra Nasional, a caompany controlled by Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, tax and tariff breaks to produce a national car in association with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
Japan, the United States and the European Union have said the policy discriminates against other manufacturers and have brought their complaint to the World Trade Organisation.
Indonesia has said the national car programme is aimed at strengthening its domestic industry.
